LESSON: PLANE GEOMETRY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: COMMUNICATION IN PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES. Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outc
Topic 2.1: Plane Geometry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Plane Geometry, part of COMMUNICATION IN PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES. Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outc in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are combined shapes applied in day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Plane Geometry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: learner acquires team working skills when discussing how to draw combined shapes.

● Learning to learn: learner develops organising skills when using available resources to construct combined shapes.

Values:
• Respect: learner appreciates diverse opinions when discussing how to draw combined shapes.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Social cohesion: learners work together harmoniously when discussing how to draw combined shapes.

Link to other subjects:

Mathematics: learner relates drawing skills to geometrical construction in Mathematics.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Print and Braille Pre-Technical Studies textbooks.

• Digital devices with assistive technology.

• Drawing books.

• Pencils.

• Geometrical instruments.

• Ruler.

• Digital devices with assistive technology such as; computer, laptop, smart phone or tablet.
